title: Calls, texts & voice notes
goal: Answer and make calls, deal with bad signal, missed calls and dead batteries, send messages, photos and your location, and say what you've just, already or not yet done.
intro:
Half of any friendship now happens on the phone: a quick call to say you're outside, a voice note because typing Pashto is slow, a missed call that means 'call me back', a location shared because nobody's street has a name anyone uses.

This unit gives you the phone Pashto people really speak — mostly Pashto verbs with English nouns (موبايل، ميس کال، لوکېشن). Grammar-wise you'll link actions in order ('get home **and then** call me', 'once I arrive, I'll text you') and use the little time words **just**, **already**, **still** and **yet**.

grammar.title: Do X and then Y: linking actions in order
grammar.body:
Pashto has no special 'having done' form. To link actions in order you have three everyday tools.

**1. Two perfective verbs with او or بيا.** Each verb takes its own perfective form: کور ته **ورسېږه** او زنګ راته **ووهه** 'get home and call me'. For a string of instructions, just chain them: ورسېږه، بيا خبر مې کړه. In the past each verb follows its own rule — so the second one can be ergative even if the first isn't: زه **ورسېدم** او زنګ **مې** ووهه 'I arrived and called'.

**2. چې + perfective = 'once, as soon as'.** Put the first action in a چې-clause with the **perfective subjunctive**: **چې** کور ته **ورسېږم**، زنګ درته وهم 'once I get home, I'll call you'. In speech the perfective past is just as common here: **چې ورسېدې**، زنګ راته ووهه 'when you've arrived, call me'.

**3. له … وروسته / له … مخکې with the verbal noun.** The infinitive is a masculine plural noun, so after له and تر it takes the oblique **-و**: رسېدل → **له رسېدو وروسته** 'after arriving', وتل → **له وتلو مخکې** 'before going out', خوړل → **تر خوړلو وروسته** 'after eating'. This is a bit more careful; in chat, option 2 is the most common.

The trap: don't use the imperfective for a one-off first step — چې کور ته **رسېږم** means 'whenever I get home' (a habit).

grammar.title: Just, already, still, yet
grammar.body:
These little words mostly go with the **present perfect** you met in unit 16 (کړی دی، راغلی يم).

**Just** — **اوس اوس** 'just now, a moment ago', with the past or the perfect: اوس اوس **راغلم** / **راغلی يم** 'I've just arrived'. (**همدا اوس** is 'right now, this very minute'.)

**Already** — **مخکې** 'already, before': ما **مخکې** ورته ويلي دي 'I've already told him'. Surprised 'already?' is **دومره ژر؟** 'so soon?'.

**Still** — **لا** or **لا هم** + a **positive** verb: **لا هم** په لار کې يم 'I'm still on the way', هغه **لا** ويده دی 'he's still asleep'.

**Yet** — **لا** or **تر اوسه** + a **negative perfect**: پيغام مې **لا** نه دی ليدلی 'I haven't seen the message yet', **تر اوسه** يې ځواب نه دی راکړی 'he hasn't replied yet'. The short answer 'not yet' is **لا نه** or **تر اوسه نه**.

**Not any more** — **نور** + negative: هغه **نور** راته زنګ نه وهي 'he doesn't call me any more'.

The traps: لا is *still* with a positive verb but *yet* with a negative one. And with a transitive verb the perfect agrees with the **object**, not with you: پيغام مې نه دی **ليدلی** (m sg) · ويډيو مې نه ده **ليدلې** (f sg) · عکسونه مې نه دي **ليدلي** (pl).

culture: Pashtuns don't skip the greetings just because it's a phone call: after **هلو** or **السلام عليکم** comes the full round — ستړي مه شې، جوړ يې، کور کې خير دی؟ — before the actual reason for calling. A **ميس کال** is a message in itself: 'call me back' (often to the friend with more credit) or 'I've arrived, come down'. **Voice notes** are everywhere, partly because many people — including plenty of fluent speakers — find typing in the Pashto script slow, and many older relatives read little or none. When people do type, young Pashtuns often write Pashto in Latin letters ('sanga ye?', 'za rawan yam') or slip into Urdu or Dari, so messages can look like a mix of three languages. In Afghanistan the networks are Roshan, AWCC, Etisalat and Salaam; in Pakistan Jazz, Zong, Telenor and Ufone. One real etiquette rule: a man doesn't phone or message a woman outside his family unless there's a clear reason (work, study) — and even then, keep it short and polite with تاسو.

tip.title: On the phone
tip.body:
- Answer with **هلو** or **السلام عليکم**, then do the usual greetings: ستړي مه شې، جوړ يې؟
- 'Can you hear me?' **غږ مې اورې؟** — 'I can't hear you': **غږ دې نه راځي** (lit. your voice isn't coming).
- To a friend use ته (اورې؟); to an elder or a stranger, تاسو (اورئ؟).

tip.title: Do X and then Y
tip.body:
- Chain perfective verbs with **او / بيا**: ورسېږه **او** زنګ راته ووهه 'get home and call me'.
- 'Once / as soon as' = **چې** + perfective: **چې** ورسېږم، زنګ درته وهم.
- 'After / before doing' = **له** + verbal noun in **-و** + وروسته / مخکې: له رسېدو وروسته، له وتلو مخکې.

lessons.title: Still waiting, not yet

tip.title: Just, already, still, yet
tip.body:
- **اوس اوس** 'just' · **مخکې** 'already' + past or perfect: اوس اوس **راغلم**.
- **لا / لا هم** + positive = **still**: لا هم ويده يې؟
- **لا / تر اوسه** + negative perfect = **yet**: لا مې نه دی ليدلی. 'Not yet' = **لا نه**.
- The perfect agrees with the object: پيغام … ليدلی · ويډيو … ليدلې · عکسونه … ليدلي.
tip.pattern: لا هم + … (still)  ·  لا / تر اوسه + نه + perfect (yet)

sentences.en: I've just got back from the office.

sentences.native: لا هم ويده يې؟ ماسپښين دی!
sentences.roman: lā ham widə́ ye? māspṣín day!
sentences.en: You're still asleep? It's the afternoon!

sentences.native: زما پيغام دې تر اوسه نه دی لوستلی؟
sentences.roman: zmā paygā́m de tər ósa na day lwastə́lay?
sentences.en: You still haven't read my message?

sentences.native: عکسونه يې تر اوسه نه دي استولي.
sentences.roman: aksúna ye tər ósa na di astawə́li.
sentences.en: He hasn't sent the photos yet.

sentences.native: موږ لا هم ستا انتظار کوو.
sentences.roman: muẓ lā ham stā intizā́r kawú.
sentences.en: We're still waiting for you.

sentences.native: ما مخکې ورته پيغام استولی دی.
sentences.roman: mā mə́xke wárta paygā́m astawə́lay day.
sentences.en: I've already sent him a message.

sentences.native: ځواب يې راکړی دی؟
sentences.roman: dzawā́b ye rā́kṛay day?
sentences.en: Has he replied?

sentences.native: لا نه، شايد بوخت دی.
sentences.roman: lā na, shāyád buxt day.
sentences.en: Not yet — maybe he's busy.

sentences.native: اوس اوس مې عکس درته واستاوه، وګوره.
sentences.roman: os os me aks dərta wā́stāwə, wə́gora.
sentences.en: I've just sent you the photo — have a look.

sentences.native: هغه نور په واټساپ کې نشته.
sentences.roman: haġá nor pə wāṭsā́p ke nə́shta.
sentences.en: He's not on WhatsApp any more.
